title: Apollo Launches £5.7 Billion Takeover Offer for easyJet, Outbidding Rivals
author: Jessica Wu
image: /images/news/Global Markets Slide as Oil Surges on Escalating Gulf Conflict.webp
excerpt: Apollo Global Management has made a surprise £5.7 billion takeover bid for easyJet, offering a higher price than rival bidder Castlelake and potentially reshaping Europe's airline industry.
content: Apollo Global Management has made a surprise £5.7 billion takeover offer for British low-cost airline easyJet, setting the stage for one of the largest aviation acquisitions in Europe this year. The all-cash proposal exceeds an earlier £5.5 billion bid submitted by investment firm Castlelake and immediately attracted the attention of investors, who pushed easyJet's shares sharply higher following the announcement. The offer represents a significant development for the European airline industry, which continues to recover from years of pandemic disruption while navigating higher operating costs, intense competition, and growing pressure to invest in more sustainable aviation technologies.

Apollo's proposal values easyJet shares at approximately £7.15 each, comfortably above Castlelake's previous offer of £6.90 per share. The airline's board confirmed that it was reviewing the latest proposal and indicated that it was inclined to recommend Apollo's bid if formal terms are finalized. Apollo has also included a "stub equity" option that would allow some existing shareholders to retain a minority interest in the airline after the acquisition, giving investors an opportunity to participate in any future growth under private ownership. Analysts said the improved offer reflects Apollo's confidence in easyJet's long-term prospects despite short-term challenges facing the aviation sector.

The takeover battle comes at a time when European airlines are benefiting from strong demand for leisure travel. Passenger numbers have continued recovering as consumers prioritize holidays and international travel despite persistent inflation and higher borrowing costs. Low-cost carriers such as easyJet have performed particularly well by attracting price-conscious travelers seeking affordable flights across Europe. However, airlines still face significant challenges, including volatile fuel prices, aircraft delivery delays, labor shortages, environmental regulations, and geopolitical tensions affecting international travel routes. These factors have made scale and financial flexibility increasingly important competitive advantages.

Apollo, one of the world's largest private equity firms, has built a reputation for acquiring businesses with strong long-term potential and improving operational performance before eventually exiting investments through public listings or strategic sales. The firm's interest in easyJet reflects growing private equity confidence in the aviation sector, particularly as airlines generate stronger earnings following the industry's recovery. Investors believe companies with recognizable brands, extensive route networks, and loyal customer bases could deliver attractive returns as global travel demand continues expanding over the coming years.

EasyJet occupies a unique position within Europe's competitive airline market. Founded in 1995, the carrier has grown into one of the continent's largest low-cost airlines, operating hundreds of aircraft and serving millions of passengers annually. Unlike some competitors that focus almost exclusively on secondary airports, easyJet maintains a strong presence at major European hubs including London Gatwick, Milan Malpensa, Geneva, and Paris Charles de Gaulle. This strategy has helped the airline attract both leisure and business travelers while maintaining strong market positions across key European destinations.

The proposed acquisition also highlights broader consolidation trends within the global airline industry. Airlines have increasingly sought mergers, acquisitions, and strategic partnerships to strengthen market share, reduce operating costs, and improve resilience against economic shocks. Rising aircraft costs, supply chain disruptions, and sustainability investments have increased pressure on carriers to achieve greater economies of scale. Private equity firms have similarly become more active in transportation and infrastructure sectors, viewing aviation as an attractive long-term investment despite its cyclical nature.

Market reaction to Apollo's proposal was overwhelmingly positive. EasyJet shares surged after news of the higher offer emerged, reflecting investor optimism that a bidding contest could further increase the company's valuation. Aviation analysts noted that competing bids often encourage higher purchase prices, benefiting shareholders while placing additional pressure on potential acquirers. Some market observers have not ruled out the possibility of further competing offers from other investment groups or strategic buyers seeking exposure to Europe's recovering aviation market.

If the acquisition proceeds, regulatory approval will represent one of the next major hurdles. Competition authorities are expected to examine the transaction carefully, although private equity ownership generally raises fewer antitrust concerns than mergers between competing airlines. Regulators will likely focus on financial stability, consumer protection, employment implications, and operational continuity rather than market concentration. Apollo has not indicated that it intends to make significant changes to easyJet's route network or customer operations, although long-term strategic decisions would likely follow after the acquisition is completed.

The proposed takeover underscores renewed confidence in the airline industry's long-term outlook after several years of unprecedented disruption. While economic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and fluctuating fuel prices continue presenting risks, passenger demand has remained resilient across many markets. For Apollo, acquiring easyJet represents an opportunity to invest in one of Europe's best-known airline brands during a period of industry transformation. For easyJet shareholders, the competing bids offer the prospect of realizing significant value while highlighting the strategic importance of the airline within Europe's highly competitive aviation landscape.
